summary: Draft Session Manager Kernel record. `TimerCheckFlags` sits under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel`, has an explicit repo-doc default of `1`, is absent on the observed clean baseline, produced an exact current-build Unicode string hit in `ntoskrnl.exe`, and has WRK-backed source-enrichment evidence that `KeTimerCheckFlags` is initialized from `KE_TIMER_CHECK_FREES` and later bit-tested in timer code. The broad lightweight runtime batch then wrote the candidate value as `1` and still returned `no-hit`. A later dedicated KVM local-KD pass resolved `nt!KeTimerCheckFlags` on the running current build and read its live value as `1`; a follow-up host-side `ntoskrnl.exe` INIT descriptor decode then bound the `Session Manager\\Kernel` `TimerCheckFlags` value-name string directly to the same `KeTimerCheckFlags` RVA. A later QGA-launched WPR boot-registry rerun then completed a real reboot, produced a 1.76 GB ETL plus a 6.06 GB tracerpt CSV, and still returned zero target hits for both the key path and `TimerCheckFlags` fragment filters. The lane is therefore live-state-confirmed and static-binding-confirmed, but even a targeted current-build boot trace still lacks an exact runtime registry read showing the boot/init descriptor path being consumed.

validation_proof.exact_quote_or_path: Docs/system/system.md assigns `TimerCheckFlags = 1` under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel`, and later string, source-enrichment, and live KD follow-ups keep the same value on the current-build research lane.
validation_proof.notes: Repo docs, baseline absence, exact current-build string presence, and the later enrichment/KD lane are enough to satisfy documentation structure; the reader/seeding path is still the real blocker.

setting.name: Timer Check Flags
setting.casual_explanation: This appears to be a kernel-level Session Manager setting tied to timer-check behavior. It is kernel-adjacent and is being tracked as a research candidate, not a user-facing tweak.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel researchers may inspect this value when investigating timer bookkeeping, timer-free validation behavior, or undocumented kernel timer diagnostics.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The value has a stronger than usual docs-first evidence chain because it has repo docs, baseline state, exact current-build string presence, WRK semantic source hits, a real write-and-reboot runtime lane, dedicated live current-build KD state, a current-build INIT descriptor binding from `TimerCheckFlags` to `KeTimerCheckFlags`, and now a targeted QGA-launched WPR boot-registry no-hit on the current build. It is still too weak for a published tweak because the exact runtime registry trace remains unresolved even after that targeted boot trace.
setting.professional_notes: Repo docs assign `TimerCheckFlags = 1` under `Session Manager\\Kernel` and map it to `KeTimerCheckFlags`. The observed clean baseline later confirmed that the parent key exists while the value itself is absent. The broad current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `TimerCheckFlags` in `ntoskrnl.exe`. Later source-enrichment over the WRK cache added stronger semantic support than a raw string hit: it retained `extern ULONG KeTimerCheckFlags;`, `ULONG KeTimerCheckFlags = KE_TIMER_CHECK_FREES;`, and a timer-object branch `if ((KeTimerCheckFlags & KE_TIMER_CHECK_FREES) == 0) {`, which strongly suggests the repo-doc default of `1` corresponds to the timer-free check bit being enabled in older kernel source. A later tools-hardened lightweight runtime lane wrote all 21 `Session Manager\\Kernel` batch values, including `TimerCheckFlags = 1`, rebooted once, preserved shell health, and still returned `no-hit` for this specific candidate in the ETW-derived query surface. A dedicated KVM local-KD follow-up then resolved `nt!KeTimerCheckFlags` and directly read its live current-build value as `1`, which aligns with both the repo-doc default and the older WRK initializer. The 2026-04-12 host-side static follow-up then decoded the current `ntoskrnl.exe` INIT descriptor row at file offset `0xBED8D8`: the row points at the `TimerCheckFlags` value-name string at VA `0x140C7BBF8` and the target global VA `0x140E0B080`. That target RVA, `0xE0B080`, matches the live KD `nt!KeTimerCheckFlags` RVA after subtracting the live kernel base. A later QGA-launched WPR boot-registry rerun then completed a real reboot, produced a 1.76 GB ETL plus a 6.06 GB tracerpt CSV, and normalized the filtered hit set successfully, but both the key-path fragment filter and the exact `TimerCheckFlags` fragment filter still returned `0` hits. The next proof step is therefore no longer symbol existence, live state, static binding, or transport reliability; it is still an exact runtime registry trace showing the boot/init descriptor path being consumed on the current build.

evidence.title: WRK source-enrichment retains KeTimerCheckFlags initialization and bit-test semantics
evidence.summary: The later source-enrichment pass retained WRK-backed hits for `extern ULONG KeTimerCheckFlags;`, `ULONG KeTimerCheckFlags = KE_TIMER_CHECK_FREES;`, and `if ((KeTimerCheckFlags & KE_TIMER_CHECK_FREES) == 0) {`, which strongly supports the repo-doc default of `1` as a timer-check bit-enabled state.

evidence.title: Lightweight runtime batch wrote TimerCheckFlags = 1 and rebooted once
evidence.summary: The tools-hardened lightweight runtime batch wrote `TimerCheckFlags = 1`, rebooted once, preserved shell health, and still returned `no-hit` for this specific candidate in the compact runtime results.

evidence.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD bundle resolves KeTimerCheckFlags = 1
evidence.summary: A dedicated live KVM local-KD bundle resolved `nt!KeTimerCheckFlags` and directly read the running current-build value as `1`.

evidence.title: Current-build INIT descriptor binds TimerCheckFlags to KeTimerCheckFlags
evidence.summary: A host-side current-build `ntoskrnl.exe` decode found the `TimerCheckFlags` UTF-16 string in the `INIT` section and one descriptor row at VA `0x140C748D8` that points to the value-name string and target global `0x140E0B080`. The target RVA `0xE0B080` matches the live KD RVA for `nt!KeTimerCheckFlags`, closing the static binding layer while leaving exact runtime registry trace evidence unresolved.

evidence.title: Boot WPR captured Session Manager Kernel QueryValue context but no exact runtime read for TimerCheckFlags
evidence.summary: A KVM boot WPR registry trace produced a saved ETL and a large tracerpt CSV. The retained context window shows `Open` for `Session Manager\\Kernel` followed by `QueryValue` for `DefaultHeteroCpuPolicy`, proving this CSV format can render exact value-name reads under the same key family. Whole-file filtering found no exact `TimerCheckFlags` hit, so this lane is retained as stronger negative runtime evidence and no exact runtime read proof.

evidence.title: Seeded default Registry-only boot WPR still found no exact runtime read for TimerCheckFlags
evidence.summary: A Registry-only WPR boot trace seeded `TimerCheckFlags = 1` before reboot, captured a saved ETL and tracerpt CSV, then rolled the value back to its original absent state. The target exact-hit filter still returned `TimerCheckFlags = 0` hits, so this is stronger negative runtime evidence and no exact runtime read proof.

evidence.title: DPC/timer ETW registry trace completed but found no TimerCheckFlags target hit
evidence.summary: A KVM guest DPC/timer ETW run collected Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Registry, Kernel-General, Kernel-Power, and Kernel-Processor-Power providers for 45 seconds, produced a 5.7 MB ETL and 57 MB tracerpt XML, and successfully uploaded the trace summary. The target filter found zero hits for `TimerCheckFlags`, so this is retained as additional negative runtime evidence and does not close the exact runtime-read blocker.

evidence.title: QGA-launched WPR boot-registry rerun completed but still found no exact TimerCheckFlags hit
evidence.summary: A QGA-launched current-build WPR boot-registry rerun completed a real reboot, saved a 1.76 GB ETL, converted it into a 6.06 GB tracerpt CSV, and normalized the filtered hit set successfully. The exact fragment filters for both `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel` and `TimerCheckFlags` still returned `0` hits, so this is stronger targeted negative runtime evidence and does not close the exact runtime-read blocker.

decision.why: The candidate is strong enough for a schema-backed draft because it has a repo-doc default, observed baseline state, current-build string hit, WRK-backed semantic source evidence, a real write-and-reboot runtime lane, dedicated live current-build KD proof that `KeTimerCheckFlags = 1`, a current-build INIT descriptor binding from `TimerCheckFlags` to the same global, and now a targeted QGA-launched WPR boot-registry rerun that completes end to end on the current build. It is not ready for validation because even that targeted boot trace still returned zero exact `TimerCheckFlags` runtime hits.
